is_anopheles.evidence: The study investigated genome-wide variation and evolution of insecticide resistance in field populations of the malaria vector Anopheles funestus across Africa (p. 1-3).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study analyzed resistance markers including GSTe2 L119F (p. 13) and the CYP6P9a/b 6.5kb structural variant insertion/deletion (p. 8-9, Table 1).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 1 lists the frequencies of the 6.5kb CYP6P9a/b structural variant across 10 pooled population samples (e.g., Mikalayi 2015 N=29 with 80% insertion, Malawi 2014 N=40 with 100% insertion, Malawi 2002 N=40 with 0% insertion). Page 13 reports GSTe2-L119F allele frequencies from PoolSeq reads (98% in Benin N=40, 31% in Ghana N=40, 27% in Cameroon N=40).

african_field_population.evidence: Wild indoor-resting blood-fed female An. funestus mosquitoes were collected from 8 African countries: Benin, Ghana, Cameroon, Uganda, DRC, Malawi, Mozambique, and Zambia between 2002 and 2016 (p. 18).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical genomic study generating and analyzing novel PoolSeq whole-genome and ddRADseq sequencing datasets.

sub_country_location.evidence: Sampling sites are specified at sub-country resolution: Kpome (Benin), Obuasi (Ghana), Mibellon (Cameroon), Tororo (Uganda), Kinshasa and Mikalayi (DRC), Chikwawa (Malawi), Palmeira/Manhica/Morrumbene (Mozambique), and Kaoma (Zambia) (p. 18, Table 1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquito collection years are explicitly specified for each location and range from single years: 2002, 2013, 2014, 2015, and 2016 (p. 18, Table 1).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Page 18 states: 'Mosquitoes were sampled from the following countries: Benin (Kpome, 2015)[9]; Ghana (Obuasi, 2014)[38]; Cameroon (Mibellon, 2015) [39]; Uganda (Tororo, 2014) [34]; Democratic Republic of Congo [Kinshasa (2015), Mikalayi (2015] [12]; Malawi (Chikwawa, 2014) [33]; Mozambique (Palmeira, 2016) [40] and Zambia (Kaoma, 2013)... Samples collected in 2002 in Chikwawa, Malawi [5] and Morrumbene, Mozambique [5] were used'. Mosquito specimens analyzed in this study were sourced from these previously published collections.

supplement.evidence: Extractable marker frequencies and sample sizes for GSTe2 L119F and CYP6P9a/b 6.5kb-SV are provided directly in the main text (p. 13) and Table 1.

assessment.summary: This study performed PoolSeq whole-genome sequencing and ddRADseq across 8 African countries to investigate population genomic structure and selective sweeps driving insecticide resistance in Anopheles funestus. It documents target resistance marker frequencies including GSTe2 L119F and structural variants at the CYP6 cluster across multiple temporal and spatial field populations.
